name: Test Coverage Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any test coverage task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any test coverage task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen test coverage approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to test coverage (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Keep test coverage changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Validate test coverage outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Document any non-obvious test coverage decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
6. When multiple test coverage strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. State assumptions about test coverage explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. When test coverage guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Prefer the simplest test coverage approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. When test coverage decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic test coverage advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated test coverage concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop test coverage edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test coverage correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for test coverage, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
